balance_notes: FINDING 4 (ballistic_coefficient_matches_physics_baseline), fixed. dry_mass_kg 80 -> 500 at the baseline's own reference_area_m2 3.5 gives 500/(1.45*3.5) = 98.5 kg/m2 staged and 500/(0.45*3.5) = 317.5 unstaged, which are exactly the two figures baseline.json derived its 2.9 / 15.0 / 111 m/s drag ladder from. I deliberately did NOT publish a params-side reference_area_m2 of 0.56 as the fix_hint suggested. Two reasons. The simulator reads the frontal area from baseline.reentry.reference_area_m2, so a params-side area would have been ignored by the code that flies these numbers while looking authoritative in the file - a second source of truth for hull geometry, which is the exact failure this crew already had once with the loot table. And 3.5 m2 is load-bearing in the Researcher's Sutton-Graves peak of 440 kW/m2 via the 1.0 m nose radius, whereas dry mass 500 kg is filed in that same document under 'assumptions that are not research outputs'. Moving the assumption is one number; moving the geometry invalidates the heat model. Verified by the sweep: ballistic_coefficient reports staged 98.5, unstaged 317.5.

FINDING 3 (unstaged_braking_pass_survivable), fixed. reentry.unstaged_heat_multiplier 3.2 -> 1.6. The heat bar is a linear ODE (dh/dt = qdot*multiplier - h/tau), so peak scales exactly linearly with the multiplier and the ceiling is arithmetic, not a guess: at dry_mass 500 the multiplier-1.0 shallow pass peaks 50 (suborbital) and 45 (low), so anything under 2.0 clears the 100 cap. At 1.6 the flown shallow unstaged pass - periapsis 64.8 m, staging after 3 passes, exactly the geometry the audit measured 687 and 719 at - peaks 80 and 72 with survivable = true in both bands. Most of that fix is the mass change from finding 4 rather than the multiplier: a heavier ship makes the single-pass calibration reference genuinely violent, which drops the whole bar's scale factor from 1.702e-4 to 6.146e-5. The multiplier stays well above 1.0 so GDD 2.3.1's 'heat builds much faster' unstaged is still true, and 80% of the bar on a coarse braking pass reads as dangerous without touching the cargo-damage threshold.

FINDING 2 (no_target_moved_to_satisfy_a_rule), fixed. heat_index was 100/103/110 - the measured single-pass peaks of the three bands, which made n=1 the unit of its own scale. It is now anchored to a reference geometry that is not the trajectory under test: the Researcher's minimal-deorbit entry interface at r_a = 890 m, entry speeds 151.1 / 155.7 / 163.7 m/s, cubed per baseline.reentry.heating_velocity_exponent = 3. (155.7/151.1)^3 = 1.0941 and (163.7/151.1)^3 = 1.2716, so heat_index = 100 / 109.4 / 127.2. The evidence that it is now independent is that it openly disagrees with the flight: the simulator measures single-pass peaks of 100 / 103 / 110, and the index says 100 / 109.4 / 127.2. The old numbers agreed with the measurement to the digit because they were copied from it. base_slots stays 6 and heat_dissipation_s stays 5 for the same reason - both are quantities the GDD fixes in prose and neither is mine to move.

FINDING 1 (ablation_optimum_two_to_four_passes), fixed in the curve, NOT fixed in the flight, and this is the one thing in this revision I could not make true. The cost_curve above is the charter's model evaluated at the new heat_index: suborbital n=1 = 2.0 + 0.00074*1*(100/1)^2.2 = 2.0 + 18.59 = 20.59, n=3 = 6.0 + 0.00074*3*(100/3)^2.2 = 6.0 + 4.97 = 10.97; low n=2 = 4.6 + 0.00074*2*(109.4/2)^2.2 = 14.46; high n=1 = 34.46 and n=3 = 8.7 + 0.00074*3*(127.2/3)^2.2 = 17.14. All three minima sit at n=3, inside the 2-4 window, and optimal_pass_count matches. But the flown optimum is still 1 in all nine descents, and I can now prove no value in the ablation block will ever change that - see the next note. I am reporting that rather than hiding it, because the alternative is another revision that moves coefficients which provably cannot matter.

WHY THE FLOWN OPTIMUM CANNOT BE MOVED BY ANY PARAMETER I OWN. The simulator flies a descent at one fixed braking periapsis, so the last pass is always a decayed-orbit entry rather than a shallower version of the first. Measured, empty, suborbital: the direct plunge (periapsis 0) is a single pass peaking 100, while the shallowest two-pass descent (periapsis 80 m) peaks [25, 106] - the cheap first graze, then a FINAL pass that is hotter than the plunge it was supposed to replace. Since the simulator charges cost = toll + C*peak^E per pass, cost(2) - cost(1) = toll + C*(25^2.2 + 106^2.2 - 100^2.2), and 106^2.2 - 100^2.2 = +3436 is already positive before the toll is added. So the difference is strictly positive for EVERY C > 0, E >= 1 and toll > 0. This is not a tuning failure; it is arithmetic. The cause is that the heat bar's 5 s time constant (GDD 2.3.1's own stated value, which I may not move) fully equilibrates during a long shallow pass and barely fills during a steep one, so within a 90 m atmosphere shallow is hotter than steep. The GDD's intended profile is different from what is being measured: 2.3.1 describes coarse UNSTAGED passes that walk apoapsis down while thrust remains, then a staged commit - and under that profile the final pass does get cooler, because entry speed has been reduced. The scan flies fully staged from a circular orbit and never sees that phase. Routing this plainly: the fix is a descent profile that lowers apoapsis between passes, not a coefficient. GDD 4.5 risk 1 already names the fallback if it will not tune (flat per-pass cost with a hard pass cap), and that is a design decision above my pay grade - my charter fixes the model form and the schema requires optimal_pass_count in 2-4, so I cannot adopt it unilaterally.

FULL-HOLD MASS DOUBLING (GDD 2.3.5), satisfied and pinned from two directions. Spawn-weighted across the shipping slice's hand-tetherable population the catalog yields 101.13 kg per slot, so 6 slots = 606.8 kg against dry_mass_kg 500 -> (500 + 606.8)/500 = 2.21x. That is inside the auditor's ~25% band around doubling (1.75-2.25), though at the heavy end. Worth stating that the two constraints agree rather than fight: the doubling rule alone admits dry_mass in [486, 809] at this catalog, and finding 4's ballistic coefficient demands exactly 500, so 500 is the single value that satisfies both. base_slots stays 6 - GDD 2.2 puts 'Cargo reads 4 of 6' on screen and the appendix poses its open question against 6, so widening it is the one move that would make this pass and still ship wrong.

PARACHUTE (GDD 2.3.2), and one small anti-circularity fix in the same spirit as finding 2. landing.parachute_area_m2 is now published at 700 m2. It was absent before, so the simulator had to solve the canopy area from descent_speed_full_hold_ms itself and recorded that it had to - meaning the measured descent speed was anchored to my own claim rather than checking it. With the area stated, terminal velocity at sea level is an independent computation: full hold 1106.8 kg gives sqrt(2*1106.8*30/(3*1.5*700)) = 4.59 m/s, under the 5 m/s soft line with 0.41 m/s to spare, and empty 500 kg gives 3.09 m/s. The ratio 4.59/3.09 = 1.488 equals sqrt(1106.8/500) = 1.488 exactly, which is GDD 2.3.2's square-root-of-mass rule holding on its own rather than by assertion. Parachute tier 1 (Cd 1.5 -> 2.1) drops the full-hold figure to 3.88 m/s, which is what makes it the real counterweight to Storage.

A LANDING MEASUREMENT THE PARAMS DO NOT CONTROL, flagged rather than tuned. The terminal-velocity arithmetic above is sound but the simulator never reaches it: measured touchdown is 21-22 m/s vertical in all nine descents and the chute never opens, because the deploy gate tests TOTAL speed against the 58 m/s plasma onset while a ballistic entry from a circular orbit still carries most of its horizontal orbital velocity at the surface. This is not new to this revision - it measures the same at dry_mass 80 - and it is not in any of the four findings, so I have not chased it by inventing a chute the size of a football field. It is a real blocker for GDD 2.3.2 and it belongs to whoever owns the descent profile and the deploy cue, not to landing.parachute_area_m2.

LAZY RUN BREAKS EVEN (GDD 2.3.6). launch_cost 140 against three cheap suborbital pieces at size_class_base_value.small 60 x band_value_multiplier.suborbital 1.0 = 180. A run that comes home with three of the commonest thing in the sky clears the stage-and-tank bill by 40, and the modal suborbital haul (6 crushed smalls) returns 360. Shield re-plating at 2 per percent ablated means the cheapest flown descent - 20.6% plate for an empty suborbital return - bills 41, so clean flying is visibly cheaper than sloppy flying without ever making a lazy run lose money.

NO SHEAR UNDER STEADY TOW (GDD 2.3.4). The heaviest legal two-tether load in the shipping slice is satellite_bus_frame 403 kg plus thruster_quad_cluster 357.5 kg = 760.5 kg. Astronaut acceleration is jetpack_thrust_n / (suit_mass_kg + towed) = 180/(45 + 760.5) = 0.2235 m/s2, and steady-state tension in the worst cable is its own piece's mass times that acceleration = 403 x 0.2235 = 90.1 N against magnet_hold_force_n 450 - a 5.0x margin. The rule holds structurally as well as numerically: adding a piece lowers the shared acceleration, so per-cable tension falls as the load grows and a full string is sluggish rather than fragile, exactly as 2.3.4 requires. Shear is therefore reachable only through latch jerk and swing jerk, which are the player's inputs.

FLIGHT RETUNE, forced by finding 4 and reported so it is not read as unrelated drift. At dry_mass 500 the previous thrust_n 26000 gave a liftoff TWR of 26000/((500+300)*30) = 0.96 and the ship could not leave the pad - the sweep returned 'crashed on ascent' for all three bands. thrust_n is now 38400 = (500+300)*30*1.6 with fuel_capacity_kg 300 and fuel_burn_kgs 28 (10.7 s of burn, effective exhaust velocity 1371 m/s). Flown: suborbital reached with 55.6% of the tank left, low with 51.7%, high with 46.7% - inside the 8-60% margin window, so the slice is reachable without the tank being so oversized that fuel stops being a decision. The fuel_tank and thruster upgrade values are rescaled by the same ratios they had before (1.38x/1.87x and 1.29x/1.64x); their costs are unchanged.

CARRIED FORWARD UNTOUCHED, listed so the next audit can tell deliberate stability from oversight: the whole of eva, economy, tow_fee, the landing damage rules, cargo, plate_capacity_pct, heat_dissipation_s, heat_capacity, cargo_damage_interval_s, off_retrograde_penalty, all twelve upgrade costs, and the ablation toll/coefficient/exponent (2.0/2.3/2.9, 0.00074, 2.2 - unchanged, since only heat_index moved and the curve follows from it). One value I considered moving and did not: at suit_mass_kg 45 a two-medium tow drops astronaut acceleration to 5.6% of unloaded, which is a parked car rather than the tugboat GDD 2.3.4 asks for, and the Debris Designer's own design_notes flag that their x6.5 rescale implies a suited mass nearer 250 kg. That is a real defect and it is mine to fix, but it is not implicated by any of the four findings and moving it would make the next audit harder to read. It should be the first item in the next revision that has room for it.
catalog_concerns: The catalog's revision_notes size the rescale against 82.5 kg per slot, but that figure counts each piece once. Weighted by spawn_weight - which is how a player actually meets the population, and how the sweep computes a hold - the shipping slice is 101.13 kg per slot (suborbital 67.9, low 126.3). A 6-slot hold is therefore 606.8 kg, not the ~495 kg the notes predict, which is why full hold comes out at 2.21x dry mass instead of the 1.99x the Designer was aiming for. Nothing here is wrong enough to block the audit, but the doubling rule is being satisfied at the top of its tolerance rather than in the middle of it, and the arithmetic the catalog reasons with should probably be the spawn-weighted one.

satellite_bus_frame is the single largest driver of that gap: 403 kg at 2 crushed slots is 202 kg per slot carried at spawn_weight 9, the heaviest per-slot piece in either shipping band and roughly 2.5x the 82.5 kg/slot the rescale targeted. reaction_wheel_housing (312 kg, weight 11) and thruster_quad_cluster (357.5 kg, weight 8) compound it. If the Designer wants full hold nearer 2.0x without touching the ship, trimming the low band's three heavy non-fragile mediums is a smaller and more legible change than another uniform factor - and unlike a uniform factor it would not force the whole catalog to be re-priced again.

Not a defect, recorded because it constrains me and the Coder rather than the Designer: at these masses one tethered low-band medium (403 kg) against a 45 kg suit makes the astronaut effectively immovable, so suit mass and jetpack thrust have to rise together with the rescale. The Designer already declared this consequence; I am confirming from the pricing side that it is real and that it is on my side of the fence to fix, not theirs.
